method: Curated, citation-backed list of large multi-year compute/capacity contracts. Every number was read from the cited url (or a second url named in the note) on 2026-11-12. confidence: 'disclosed' = stated by a party (press release, blog or SEC filing); 'reported' = not disclosed by the companies, taken from reputable press as noted. Most values are 'up to' ceilings subject to delivery, availability and termination conditions, not guaranteed payments. term_years is the stated term where there is one; for CoreWeave rows it is the span from signing to the stated end date, noted per row. Implied $/GPU-hr is computed only when value, term and GPU count for the same contract are all disclosed or reported: value / (gpus x 8760 x years), or monthly fee x 12 / (gpus x 8760). It assumes every GPU is billed for the whole term (deliveries are often phased, which would raise the true rate) and includes everything the contract bundles (networking, storage, CPUs, power, data center, services), so it is an upper bound on pure GPU cost. Rows with an implied price have confidence 'estimate'; their inputs are disclosed figures. GPU counts are never inferred from MW. Colocation leases (Fluidstack rows) are power/space, not compute, and must not be compared with GPU-hour prices. Rows for the same buyer and seller can overlap (CoreWeave-OpenAI tranches sum to the ~$22.4B CoreWeave reported; the Nscale Narvik row may be inside the Nscale $43.8B aggregate).

items.source: CoreWeave press release; CoreWeave S-1/A (Mar 2025) and 10-Q
items.note: 'Up to approximately $11.9 billion through October 2030', subject to delivery/availability requirements; 'up to' ceiling. term_years = span from signing (Mar 2025) to stated end date (Oct 2030). OpenAI also received $350M of CoreWeave stock. Press release: https://coreweave.com/news/coreweave-announces-agreement-with-openai-to-deliver-ai-infrastructure

'As of May 14, 2025 ... OpenAI has committed to pay the Company up to $4.0 billion through April 2029.' No standalone press release; counterparty first unnamed on the earnings call. term_years = span May 2025 to Apr 2029.

Order form signed 2025-09-23 under MSA dated 2025-05-08: 'up to approximately $6.5 billion through May 31, 2031'. Press release says this brings total OpenAI contract value to up to ~$22.4B (11.9 + 4.0 + 6.5); do not sum with the earlier rows as a separate deal. term_years = span Sep 2025 to May 2031.

Order form signed 2025-09-25: Meta 'initially committed to pay the Company up to approximately $14.2 billion through December 14, 2031', with an option to materially expand through 2032. GPU type not in the filing (press reports said GB300; not verified here). term_years = span Sep 2025 to Dec 2031.

items.gpu_type: NVIDIA Vera Rubin (includes some initial deployments)
items.note: Press release (https://coreweave.com/news/coreweave-and-meta-announce-21-billion-expanded-ai-infrastructure-agreement, dated 2026-04-09) says ~$21B through December 2032. The 10-Q says the order form was entered in March 2026 and the 'up to approximately $21.0 billion' includes new capacity through 2032-12-20 and the exercise of the existing option from the Sept 2025 order form through 2032-04-10. Neither source says whether it overlaps the $14.2B order; treat it as additional but unconfirmed. term_years = span Apr 2026 to Dec 2032.

Dedicated GPU capacity at Vineland, NJ, over a five-year term, deployed in tranches during 2025-2026; 'total contract value is about $17.4 billion through 2031', rising to ~$19.4B if Microsoft buys additional services/capacity. Obligations start once Nebius confirms financing. GPU count/type not disclosed.
'A new agreement to deliver AI infrastructure to Meta valued at approximately $3 billion over 5 years.' No GPU or MW detail.

Agreement signed 2026-03-13. Value is 'up to approximately $27 billion': $12B of firm 5-year dedicated GPU cluster orders (tranches starting early 2027, including storage and connectivity), plus up to $15B in which Meta must buy capacity Nebius does not sell to third parties for 5 years from deployment. The $15B part is contingent, so firm value is $12B.

Partner Statement of Work signed 2025-11-02: ~$9.7B through 2031, five-year average term, 20% prepayment per tranche; Horizon 1-4 at Childress, TX, ~200MW combined IT load; tranches targeted for 2026. ~$5.8B GPU and equipment capex (Dell). IREN presentation gives ~$1.94B ARR. GPU count not disclosed.

items.source: Microsoft Source EMEA (value, term); Nscale press release 2025-10-15 (GPU count)
items.note: Microsoft: five-year agreement 'worth an estimated $6.2 billion', services in stages from 2026, Narvik, Norway. The GPU count comes from a different source: Nscale's 2025-10-15 release (https://nscale.com/press-releases/nscale-microsoft-2025) says the Aker-Nscale JV 'signed a multi-year agreement to deliver approximately 52,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs to Microsoft' at Narvik. Implied price assumes all 52,000 GPUs run the full 5 years, though deliveries are staged. Can overlap the Nscale $43.8B aggregate row. Confidence is 'estimate' because of the implied price; the value, term and GPU inputs are company-disclosed.

items.gpu_type: NVIDIA GB300 and Vera Rubin NVL72
items.note: Aggregate of Microsoft statements of work signed September 2025 to April 2026: 'up to approximately $43.8 billion through December 2033', excluding optional extensions. Covers GPU infrastructure, colocation space and cloud services. GPU service terms run 5-6 years from acceptance of each tranche, so term_years is left null. Date is the S-1 filing that disclosed the value. Underlying announcements: ~200,000 GB300 (Texas ~104k, Narvik ~52k, Loughton ~23k, Sines ~12.6k) on 2025-10-15, plus >66,000 Vera Rubin at Sines from late 2027. Mapping of GPUs to SOWs is not disclosed, so no implied price. Earlier press estimates: Bloomberg ~$23B (2025-11-04), FT ~$14B, CNBC/FT up to $24B; superseded by this filing.

Four GPU Services Agreements signed 2026-08-25 for dedicated GPU infrastructure at the Monarch Compute Campus, Mason County, WV: 'aggregate payments to us of up to approximately $44.6 billion', across four tranches, each 'multi-year' from acceptance with extension options. As of the S-1, Nscale had no binding financing commitments. Anthropic can terminate a tranche without liability if it is late. Monarch: initial ~1.37GW IT load targeted for H1 2028. GPU count and term not disclosed.

$38B multi-year agreement 'which will have continued growth over the next seven years'. term_years = 7 from that wording, not a stated contract term. Covers 'hundreds of thousands' of NVIDIA GPUs (no exact count), with all targeted capacity deployed before end of 2026.

Expands the existing $38B agreement 'by $100 billion over 8 years'. OpenAI to consume ~2GW of Trainium capacity (Trainium4 delivery expected from 2027). Announced with Amazon's investment in OpenAI. Accelerators are Trainium, not GPUs.
'OpenAI has contracted to purchase an incremental $250B of Azure services.' Part of the recapitalization agreement. No term or capacity disclosed. 'Azure services' is broader than GPU compute.

'Anthropic has committed to purchase $30 billion of Azure compute capacity', plus additional capacity up to one gigawatt contracted separately (not in the $30B). No term disclosed. Announced with NVIDIA and Microsoft investments in Anthropic.

items.source: Wall Street Journal report, confirmed by CNBC
items.note: Neither company disclosed the value. WSJ reported, and CNBC confirmed, ~$300B of compute over about five years starting 2027. The 4.5GW is OpenAI's own Stargate-with-Oracle figure (July 2025). Oracle's 8-K (2025-06-30, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1341439/000119312525152035/d136779d8k.htm) disclosed an unnamed contract 'expected to contribute more than $30 billion in annual revenue starting in FY28'; press widely attributed it to OpenAI.

items.source: The Information, via Reuters; Data Centre Review
items.note: Reported 'more than $10 billion over six years' for Google Cloud servers, storage, networking and other services; value is a floor. Not confirmed by either company. Date is the approximate original report date (Reuters, ~2025-08-21).

items.source: OpenAI/Cerebras announcement; value from sources via Bloomberg and The Register
items.note: Companies announced 750MW of Cerebras-hosted compute built in stages 'through 2028'. Value not disclosed; people familiar put it at 'over $10B', so it is a floor. term_years null (only 'through 2028'). Accelerators are not GPUs.

items.gpu_type: NVIDIA (mixed, incl. GB200; COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II)
items.note: Deal announced 2026-05-06 (Colossus 1), expanded ~2026-05-20 to Colossus II. Prospectus: compute 'includes approximately 325,000 NVIDIA GPUs'; Anthropic 'has agreed to pay us $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with capacity ramping in May and June 2026 at a reduced fee'. After the first three months either party may terminate on 90 days' notice, so value_usd_bn is null (press estimates of ~$40-45B assume no termination). Implied price uses the full monthly fee over 325,000 GPUs (8760/12 hours per month) and also covers CPUs, exabyte-scale storage and networking. Confidence is 'estimate' because of the implied price; the value, term and GPU inputs are company-disclosed.

items.source: Volta announcement; customer reported by Bloomberg (via The Decoder)
items.note: Volta announced a $10B, six-year compute commitment from an unnamed AI lab: 133MW at Tydal, Norway (co-developed with Bitdeer), handed over in two phases through March 2027. Bloomberg reported the customer as Anthropic; neither company confirmed. No GPU count.

Colocation (data center lease), not GPU compute. Two 10-year HPC colocation leases at Lake Mariner, NY: >200MW critical IT, ~$3.7B contracted revenue (~$8.7B with two 5-year extensions). Google backstops $1.8B of Fluidstack's obligations and gets ~8% equity in TeraWulf via warrants. Do not compare with GPU-hour prices.

items.source: Cipher Mining 8-K and press release Ex. 99.1
items.note: Colocation (data center lease), not GPU compute. 10-year HPC colocation at Barber Lake, Colorado City, TX: 168MW critical IT, delivery by Sept 2026, ~$3B contracted revenue (~$7B with two 5-year extensions). Google backstops $1.4B and gets ~5.4% equity via warrants.

Colocation (data center lease), not GPU compute. Lease signed 2025-09-26, announced 2025-10-28: 168MW critical IT at Abernathy, TX, delivery H2 2026, 25-year term (Fluidstack may shorten to 20 or 15 years), ~$9.5B contracted 25-year revenue to the JV. Google backstops Fluidstack's lease obligations.
